angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 598,302 km at 185.56 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.3891 +/- 0.0263 mas (same row, RUWE 1.68): 185.56 pc, no zero-point correction; the RUWE is high, so the astrometry fits a single star poorly, and the parallax is used as published
radiusSource: Radius 0.86 +/- 0.01 solar radii from Livingston et al. 2018, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-279 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156..277L/abstract): 598,302 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.79 +/- 0.03 solar masses from Livingston et al. 2018, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-279 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156..277L/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5558 +/- 70 K from Livingston et al. 2018, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-279 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156..277L/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Livingston et al. 2018, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-279 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156..277L/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-279.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.467, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
